_mineralFields: Worlds since terrainGen 15 (Terrain._mineralFields): the things you mine lie in a few ore fields, not in every hill, so one land has iron and coal and must buy its silver and salt from another. Each mineral gets perRoot fields per square root of the world's land hexes (at least min), placed apart (spacing in hexes, x the map's scale) on the land it likes (centre: terrain ids a field may be centred on; on: terrain ids that carry the mineral inside a field). A field is radius hexes across (x the map's scale, sqrt(land)/64), and a hex of the right land in it carries the mineral at core chance in its heart, falling to edge at its rim. Outside its fields a mineral is not found at all: not as a map resource, not as a hidden vein, not by prospecting. Stone, timber, fish, farmland, herds and spices are not minerals: they stay everywhere. Copper and silver are map resources only in these worlds.
_coasts: Worlds since terrainGen 16 (Terrain._fjords16, Terrain._shores16): coasts with character. fjords: on cold coasts (latitude at least minLatitude, 0 equator .. 1 pole, and the hex's temperature at most maxTemp) where high ground (hills and up) meets the open sea, perMap fjords (x the map's scale, sqrt(hexes/9600)) are cut, each a winding inlet of minLength..maxLength hexes inland, every hex with at least highFlanks high hexes beside it, mouths at least spacing hexes apart (x scale), the water depth below sea level (so it is Coastal Waters, which ships sail); tries mouths per fjord wanted are tried. An inlet never reaches another sea or a lake, never runs over a river and never cuts land off. beaches: shore land by the sea at most maxRise above sea level, temperature at least minTemp, not on notOn terrain and with no hill behind it, becomes Beach in runs of runMin..runMax hexes, a run starting at a shore hex with seedChance; steep coasts stay rocky. skerries: one-hex Island islets in open water within reach hexes of rocky shore (rocky terrain ids), at chance per hex (nearFjord within reach of a fjord), never touching the shore, a fjord, another islet or a river's mouth; each keeps its fishing ground.
_wetlands: Worlds since terrainGen 16 (Terrain._wetlands16): marshes on flat, wet, low ground. A land hex of one of the 'on' terrains no more than lowBand above sea level (lowBand + waterBand beside a river, lake or sea), with moisture of minMoisture or more (wetBonus less beside a river or lake) and temperature of minTemp or more can be marsh; below coldTemp it is a cold bog, its score cut by coldPenalty, so the tundra latitudes have few. The wettest, lowest hexes seed patches: patchesPerLand x the land hexes x the rainfall factor (rainfall: arid..tropical) of them, no two within patchSpacing hexes, each grown out over its eligible neighbours (the eligibility relaxed by grow) to patchMin..patchMax hexes; a patch that cannot reach patchMin is not laid. Score: moisture, + riverBonus on a river, + lakeBonus beside a lake, + seaBonus by a river's mouth, - the height above the sea over lowBand x lowPenalty, + up to jitter at random. delta: the maxDeltas (per 120x80 of map, at least 1) biggest rivers fed by minFeed river hexes or more that reach the sea within maxRise of sea level on flat land, no two within spacing hexes, get a delta: their mouth and up to fan low land hexes beside it and the hex above it become marsh, and where a low land hex beside the mouth (or the hex above it) touches the sea elsewhere, the river splits there (tile.riverBranch: the second way out, the distributary hex flows to the sea) when branch is true.
_passes: Worlds since terrainGen 16 (Terrain._passes16): a long mountain range is a wall with gateways. Ranges are connected bands of mountain and snow peak at least minRangeHexes big whose spine (the longest walk along them) is at least minRangeLength hexes; such a range gets one pass per hexesPerPass of spine (at most maxPerRange), where good lowland (plains and hills, in a lowland at least minLowland hexes big) lies on both sides within window hexes, in a strip strip hexes either side of the crossing. Each pass follows the lowest saddle across (a search on height, with jitter so it bends like a notch, not a cut), no closer to another pass of its range than spacing x (spine / passes) along it, nor than apart hexes to its climb. The hexes it crosses are set to highlands at the crest (crest: 0 the highlands floor .. 1 the mountain line) falling to hills at its feet (foot: 0 the hills floor .. 1 the highlands line); the mountains beside it are pulled down toward the mountain line by shoulder (0 none .. 1 all the way), so its flanks are bare rock, not snow.
